core_obligations: Direct direction: $f$ an immersion implies each $f_i$ an immersion by base change of immersions, proving the direct implication of the definition (proof lines 2253-2260).

Converse setup: each $f_i$ immersion implies each $f_i$ separated (immersions are monomorphisms) and locally quasi-finite (immersions are locally quasi-finite); descend separated and locally quasi-finite to $f$ by the chapter's descent lemmas (proof lines 2260-2271).
Pivot: a separated locally quasi-finite morphism of algebraic spaces is representable (proof lines 2271-2275).

Reduce: it suffices to show $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is an immersion for every scheme $Z \to Y$ (criterion for closed immersion locality); refine the pullback of the covering $\{Y_i \to Y\}$ by an fppf covering $\{Z_i \to Z\}$ of schemes (proof lines 2277-2287).

Conclude: $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is a morphism of schemes which becomes an immersion after the fppf pullback to the $Z_i$, hence is an immersion by the scheme-side descent lemma (proof lines 2287-2293).
proof_roadmap: Prove the direct direction by base change.
Extract separated and locally quasi-finite from the $f_i$ and descend them.
Conclude representability of $f$ from separated plus locally quasi-finite.
Test on schemes over the base after refining the fppf covering by schemes, and apply the scheme-side descent lemma.
difficulty_reason: The converse direction is a genuine multi-step argument: from $f_i$ immersions it extracts separated and locally quasi-finite via two cited implications, descends both properties with the chapter's descent lemmas, and reaches the pivot that $f$ is representable; then it reduces to testing on schemes $Z \to Y$, refines the fppf covering by schemes, and concludes with the scheme-side descent of immersions.
